content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
Maester is a PowerShell framework that checks Microsoft 365 security configuration. The defender's path (design accepted 5 November 2026, docs/proposals/defenders-path.md) orders fixes the way Microsoft Learn documents: what must be in place first, what a fix unlocks, and whether the tenant is ready. Tests name the step they verify with a Step attribute, and a catalogue in powershell/assets/steps holds the steps, their relationships (Requires, RequiresOneOf, RecommendedFirst, Conflicts, OnlyWhen), their rollout and their cited Learn sources. Goals group steps into lanes.

Milestone M1 (draft PR maester365/maester#2683, branch feat/defenders-path) shipped the format, the loader and checks, and the compliant-devices goal with seven steps. While building M1, a Learn check showed that compliant devices must be registered and enrolled, not joined, so its readiness step is intune.devices-compliant.

Owner rulings to respect: the attribute is Step, lanes are Goals, the catalogue lives in powershell/assets/steps, the wording is our own with a link, and no test re-implements another suite's check (a benchmark duplicate is a shim). A separate session has already made CIS.M365.4.1 a shim of MT.1054 on another branch, so leave that test's body alone.

Task:
Build milestone M2 of the defender's path: the step catalogue for the seven goals, checked against Microsoft Learn, with the verifying tests tagged.

Read first: `docs/proposals/defenders-path.md` (sections 3–5, 14, 15 and 16), then the M1 code it builds on: `powershell/assets/steps/` (schema, `goals.json`, `entra.json`, `intune.json`), `powershell/internal/engine/Get-MtStepCatalog.ps1`, `Get-MtStepProblem.ps1`, and the tests `powershell/tests/functions/engine/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1` and `powershell/tests/general/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`. Also follow `AGENTS.md`.

Work:
1. Expert pass. For each goal in section 15's table (compliant devices, risk policies, phishing-resistant MFA, privileged access, token protection, email authentication, Defender risk in compliance), confirm every step and every relationship against Learn. Use the public mirrors `merill/entra-docs-mirror`, `intune-docs-mirror`, `defender-docs-mirror`, `security-docs-mirror`, `purview-docs-mirror`, `teams-docs-mirror`, `sharepoint-docs-mirror`, `exchange-docs-mirror` and `windows-server-docs-mirror` (shallow clones are fine), or fetch any Learn page as Markdown with `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown'`. Section 15 is a draft. Change steps, order or relationships where Learn says otherwise, and drop a relationship that Learn doesn't back unless you cite a maintainer source (keep those rare).
2. Write the steps into `powershell/assets/steps/<product>.json` and the goals into `goals.json`. Every `Note` is Maester's own wording, at most 200 characters, never copied Learn text. URLs have no locale. `Reviewed` is today's date.
3. Tag the verifying tests with `Step`. Read each test's code before tagging. Tests whose definition of done differs (a stricter or narrower setting) get separate steps, as section 5 explains for CIS 5.2.2.9 against MT.1001. Shims must carry the same `Step` as the test they call (`TestShims.Tests.ps1`).
   - EIDSCA (`tests/eidsca`) and ORCA tests are generated. Never hand-edit them. Either add `Step` support to the generators (`build/eidsca/`, `build/orca/`) and regenerate, or leave them out and list them in your report.
   - Steps that only the Zero Trust pack checks keep `Unchecked`, naming the ZTA IDs.
   - Two readiness steps stay `Unchecked` because a separate session is writing their checks: `intune.devices-compliant` and `entra.mfa-registered`. Add `entra.mfa-registered` to the catalogue as a step, but don't write checks for it.
4. Update section 15 of the design doc to match what you found, with step counts. You are the only session editing `powershell/assets/steps/` and the doc. Others are working in parallel on new readiness-check test files (M5) and on `build/steps/` tooling (M6).

Done means: the seven goals are in the catalogue, `Get-MtStepProblem -Coverage` reports nothing, `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` and `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` pass, and the work is committed on your branch. Ask the user before pushing or opening a PR. It would be a draft PR for Maester 3.1, based on `feat/defenders-path`, because main is in the 3.0 code freeze from 7 November 2026. Report what changed from the draft table and why, with the Learn pages you relied on.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/merill/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_dfb877c0-85e7-4697-9748-c3171aca3375

1	# Design: the defender's path
2	
3	> **Status: accepted for implementation, 2026-11-05.** The owner accepted every recommendation in section 17.
4	> Targets Maester 3.1: main is in the 3.0 code freeze from 7 November 2026.
5	
6	## 1. Summary
7	
8	Attack-path tools show the route an attacker takes. The defender's path shows the order a defender has to work
9	in: what has to be in place before a fix works, what a fix unlocks, and whether the tenant is ready for it.
10	Microsoft Learn documents this order page by page, but no assessment tool uses it. The owner ruled on 5 November
11	2026 that it should be Maester's strong point.
12	
13	The design adds four things:
14	
15	- **A catalogue of steps.** A step is one change an administrator makes ("Assign a compliance policy for each
16	  platform") or one state the tenant must reach ("Devices that sign in are compliant"). The catalogue says
17	  how steps relate (requires, requires one of, only when, recommended first, conflicts) and how to switch each
18	  one on. Every relationship cites Microsoft Learn in Maester's own words. Goals group the steps that lead to
19	  one outcome, such as "Require compliant devices".
20	- **A `Step` attribute on tests.** A test names the step it verifies. Tests in different suites that check the
21	  same setting name the same step, so CIS, CISA, Maester and Zero Trust checks fall into one place.
22	- **`Steps` and `Goals` in the result.** For every step in scope the engine works out its status (Done, Not
23	  done, Unknown, Not checked, Not applicable), whether it can start (Ready, Blocked, Unconfirmed), what blocks
24	  it and what it unlocks, and its place in the order. The report, the console, CSV and Markdown all read
25	  these. None of them works the order out again.
26	- **Readiness checks.** These are new tests for prerequisites that are states rather than settings, such as the
27	  share of Windows devices that are joined. They report a count and pass above a threshold.
28	
29	A run without any test that names a step looks exactly as it does today.
30	
31	## 2. The problem
32	
33	The action plan ranks failed tests by severity, user impact and implementation cost (`priority()` in
34	`report/src/lib/model.ts`). It knows nothing about order. In a tenant with no Intune compliance policies it can
35	put MT.1001 ("At least one Conditional Access policy is configured with device compliance") near the top.
36	Following that advice before devices are enrolled and covered by compliance policies locks users out. The
37	guide for MT.1001 says only "Review the configuration described above."
38	
39	Microsoft Learn is explicit about the order for this change and many others:
40	
41	| Change | What Learn says comes first |
42	| --- | --- |
43	| Require a compliant device in Conditional Access | An Intune compliance policy, and at least one compliant device, before the policy is on |
44	| User-risk and sign-in-risk policies | Users registered for MFA, and password writeback for synced users. Remediate existing risky users first |
45	| Token protection | Windows devices joined or registered, Apple devices managed with the SSO plug-in. Pilot in report-only |
46	
47	Three things make this hard to bolt onto the current model:
48	
49	- Several suites check the same setting. MT.1001 and ZTA.24824 both check that Conditional Access requires a
50	  compliant device. Prerequisites tagged on each test would be repeated and would drift.
51	- Many prerequisites are not settings. "Devices are enrolled" is a state of the tenant, so it needs its own
52	  node and often its own check.
53	- Some prerequisites have alternatives, and some apply only to some tenants. Password writeback, for example,
54	  matters only for synced users.
55	
56	So the unit is the change, not the test: tests point at a step, and the catalogue holds the facts. This is the
57	model the framework files already use. The mapping lives on the test's `Control`, and
58	`tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json` holds the requirements.
59	
60	## 3. Terms
61	
62	| Term | Meaning |
63	| --- | --- |
64	| Step | One change or one tenant state, with an ID such as `intune.compliance-policies` |
65	| Prerequisite | A step that another step requires, requires one of, or recommends first |
66	| Goal | An outcome and the step that achieves it, such as "Require compliant devices". Its steps are that step and its prerequisites, followed down every level |
67	| Readiness check | A test whose step is a tenant state. It reports a share and passes above a threshold |
68	| Verifying tests | The tests whose `Step` names a step |
69	
70	The name shown to readers is "Defender's path". In the report it reads as "Defender's path · Require compliant
71	devices · 3 of 7 steps done".
72	
73	## 4. The catalogue
74	
75	### 4.1 Files
76	
77	```
78	powershell/assets/steps/
79	  goals.json        the goals, in the order the report shows them
80	  entra.json        the steps whose Product is entra
81	  intune.json
82	  exchange.json
83	  defender.json
84	  ...               one file per product key that has steps
85	```
86	
87	The catalogue ships in the module beside the taxonomy registry and is read at run time, so it needs no build
88	step. Files are split by product to keep merge conflicts small. A step's file is named after the product in its
89	ID.
90	
91	Each file has this shape:
92	
93	```json
94	{
95	  "$schema": "./steps.schema.json",
96	  "Product": "entra",
97	  "Steps": [ ]
98	}
99	```
100	
101	`powershell/assets/steps/steps.schema.json` describes both file types so that editors validate as you type.
102	
103	### 4.2 A step
104	
105	```json
106	{
107	  "Id": "entra.ca-require-compliant-device",
108	  "Title": "Require a compliant device in Conditional Access",
109	  "Summary": "Sign-ins from devices Intune does not mark compliant are blocked.",
110	  "Requires": ["intune.compliance-policies", "intune.devices-compliant", "entra.emergency-access-excluded", "entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts"],
111	  "RequiresOneOf": [],
112	  "RecommendedFirst": ["intune.mark-unassigned-noncompliant"],
113	  "Conflicts": [],
114	  "OnlyWhen": [],
115	  "Rollout": [
116	    "Create the policy in report-only mode and review the sign-ins it would block.",
117	    "Turn it on for a pilot group.",
118	    "Turn it on for all users, keeping the emergency access accounts excluded."
119	  ],
120	  "Sources": [
121	    {
122	      "Url": "https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance",
123	      "Mirror": "entra-docs-mirror",
124	      "Note": "Create an Intune compliance policy first, and have at least one compliant device, or the policy blocks everyone.",
125	      "Reviewed": "2026-11-05"
126	    }
127	  ]
128	}
129	```
130	
131	| Field | Required | Rule |
132	| --- | --- | --- |
133	| `Id` | yes | `<product-key>.<name>`. The product key comes from the taxonomy, and the name is lowercase kebab-case. Stable once shipped, like a test ID |
134	| `Title` | yes | Imperative for a change ("Require…", "Assign…"), a statement for a state ("Devices that sign in are compliant"). One line |
135	| `Summary` | yes | One sentence on what changes for users or the tenant |
136	| `Requires` | no | Steps that must be done first, or the change fails or locks users out |
137	| `RequiresOneOf` | no | Groups of at least two steps. Any one step in a group is enough |
138	| `RecommendedFirst` | no | Steps that make this one safer or more useful. They never block |
139	| `Conflicts` | no | Steps that must be off before this one can be on. Declared on the step that needs the other one off |
140	| `OnlyWhen` | no | Conditions from section 4.4. All must hold, or the step is Not applicable |
141	| `Rollout` | no | Ordered sentences on how to switch it on safely |
142	| `Sources` | yes | At least one. See section 4.5 |
143	| `Unchecked` | when no test names the step | Why Maester cannot check it yet, in one sentence |
144	
145	A step has no severity, cost or licence of its own. Those stay on its verifying tests, so they are never
146	declared twice.
147	
148	### 4.3 Relationships
149	
150	| Relationship | Meaning | Effect on the plan | Example |
151	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
152	| Requires | Must be done first | Blocks the step while the prerequisite is Not done | Compliant-device CA requires compliance policies |
153	| RequiresOneOf | Any one of a group will do | Blocks the step while every step in the group is Not done | A managed-device grant is met by a compliant device or a hybrid joined one |
154	| RecommendedFirst | Works without it, but is safer after it | Orders only, never blocks | Remediate high-risk users (MT.1260) before the user-risk policy |
155	| Conflicts | The other step must be off first | Blocks the step while the conflicting step is Done | Conditional Access policies can't be turned on while security defaults are on |
156	| OnlyWhen | Applies to some tenants only | Not applicable when a condition is false | Password writeback, only for hybrid identity |
157	| Rollout | How to switch it on | Shown in How to fix | Report-only, a pilot group, then everyone |
158	
159	### 4.4 Conditions
160	
161	`OnlyWhen` takes keys from a closed list, so that the engine can evaluate every condition without running a
162	check:
163	
164	| Condition | True when | Read from |
165	| --- | --- | --- |
166	| `hybrid-identity` | The tenant syncs identities from on-premises | `onPremisesSyncEnabled` on the organization, which the tenant context already reads |
167	| `license:<service plan>` | The tenant has the service plan, written as in a test's `License` | The licences the tenant context already reads |
168	
169	If a condition cannot be read, for example because Graph is not connected, the step is Unknown, not Not
170	applicable. New conditions are added to this list and to the engine together.
171	
172	### 4.5 Sources and wording
173	
174	- `Url` is the Learn page with no locale, the form the check guides use.
175	- `Mirror` names the Learn mirror repository that holds the page, out of the nine `merill/*-docs-mirror`
176	  repositories. The tooling of section 13 finds the file from the URL, so the path is not written by hand.
177	- `Note` is Maester's own wording of what the page says about order, up to 200 characters. Never copy
178	  Microsoft's text.
179	- `Reviewed` is the date someone last read the page against the step. The change-detection workflow compares
180	  it with the mirror's history.
181	- A relationship that Learn does not document can cite a maintainer instead:
182	  `{ "Maintainer": "merill", "Note": "...", "Reviewed": "..." }`. The unit tests count these, and the review keeps
183	  them rare.
184	
185	### 4.6 Goals
186	
187	```json
188	{
189	  "Goals": [
190	    {
191	      "Id": "compliant-devices",
192	      "Title": "Require compliant devices",
193	      "Summary": "Only devices that Intune manages and marks compliant can reach Microsoft 365.",
194	      "Step": "entra.ca-require-compliant-device"
195	    }
196	  ]
197	}
198	```
199	
200	A goal's steps are not listed. They are its `Step` plus everything that step requires, requires one of, or
201	recommends first, followed down every level. A step can belong to several goals. For example,
202	`entra.emergency-access-excluded` sits under compliant devices, risk policies and privileged access. Goal IDs are lowercase
203	kebab-case with no product prefix, because a goal often spans products.
204	
205	## 5. The `Step` attribute
206	
207	```powershell
208	[MaesterTest(
209	    Id      = 'MT.1001',
210	    Title   = 'At least one Conditional Access policy is configured with device compliance.',
211	    Product = 'entra',
212	    Feature = 'conditional-access',
213	    Step    = 'entra.ca-require-compliant-device',
214	    ...
215	)]
216	```
217	
218	| Property | Type | Values | Built-in tests | Notes |
219	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
220	| `Step` | string[] | step IDs | optional | Usually one value, at most three. Pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`, at most 80 characters. Stored in lowercase |
221	
222	- It is added to `MaesterTestAttribute` in `src/Maester.Engine` and to `powershell/assets/MaesterTestSchema.psd1`
223	  together, since a unit test compares them. The DLL in `powershell/lib/` is rebuilt.
224	- A built-in test must name steps that exist in the catalogue, or the build fails. A custom test or a pack test
225	  may name any built-in step. A step ID the catalogue does not have stays on the row with a warning and is left
226	  out of `Steps`. Custom catalogues are not part of this design (section 18).
227	- A family instance can set `Step` the way it sets `Product` and `Feature` on the
228	  `feat/zta-taxonomy-mapping` branch (`Get-MtInstanceAttribute`). The Zero Trust pack takes each test's
229	  steps from its hand-kept `taxonomy.json`, next to `AlsoCheckedBy`.
230	- Pester-format tests have no `Step`.
231	- Tests with different definitions of done get different steps, even when they read the same setting. CIS
232	  5.2.2.9 accepts a compliant or a hybrid joined device. MT.1001 needs device compliance. So CIS 5.2.2.9 names
233	  `entra.ca-require-managed-device` and MT.1001 names `entra.ca-require-compliant-device`. Otherwise one step
234	  would pass and fail in the same run.
235	- `Step` is not a taxonomy tag and adds no tag. `Get-MtTest -Step` and `Invoke-Maester -Step` select by it
236	  (section 8).
237	
238	## 6. A step's status in a run
239	
240	### 6.1 Status
241	
242	A step's status comes from the results of its verifying tests in this run. A test the run did not select
243	counts as not run.
244	
245	| Status | Rule, checked in this order |
246	| --- | --- |
247	| Not applicable | An `OnlyWhen` condition is false, or every verifying test that ran was skipped as `NotApplicable` |
248	| Not done | Any verifying test failed |
249	| Unknown | No test failed, and at least one ended as Investigate, Error or Skipped. The reason codes are kept |
250	| Done | At least one verifying test passed, and every test that ran passed |
251	| Not checked | No verifying test ran. `Reason` is `NotSelected` when tests exist and `NoCheck` when none do (the step is `Unchecked`) |
252	
253	Done means done as far as this run checked. The step record says how many of its tests ran ("1 of 2 checks
254	ran"). The three statuses Not done, Unknown and Not checked never blur. Unknown says the run could not tell,
255	Not checked says it did not look, and neither is counted as Not done.
256	
257	### 6.2 Readiness
258	
259	Readiness applies to steps that are Not done, Unknown or Not checked. Prerequisites that are Not applicable
260	count as met.
261	
262	| Readiness | Rule |
263	| --- | --- |
264	| Blocked | A `Requires` step is Not done, every step of a `RequiresOneOf` group is Not done, or a `Conflicts` step is Done. `BlockedBy` lists them |
265	| Unconfirmed | Not blocked, but a prerequisite is Unknown or Not checked. `Unconfirmed` lists them |
266	| Ready | Every `Requires` step is Done and every `RequiresOneOf` group has a step that is Done |
267	
268	`RecommendedFirst` never changes readiness. It appears as "Recommended first" with the step's status.
269	
270	### 6.3 Order
271	
272	Steps get a `Rank` so that every output lists them in the same order:
273	
274	1. **Group:** Ready, then Unconfirmed, then Blocked. Within the Unconfirmed group, the prerequisites to check
275	   come right before the steps they would confirm.
276	2. **Dependencies:** `Requires`, `RequiresOneOf` and `RecommendedFirst` edges, in topological order. The unit
277	   tests guarantee that the graph has no cycles.
278	3. **Value:** a step's own value is the highest `priority()` among its failed tests. Its unlock value is the sum
279	   of the values of the Not done steps that depend on it, at any depth. "Enroll devices in Intune" therefore
280	   ranks by the controls it enables, not by its own severity.
281	4. **ID**, so the order is stable.
282	
283	`priority()` moves from the report into the engine as `Get-MtTestPriority`, so that the console and Markdown rank
284	the same way. The report keeps its copy for results that have no `Steps`. A unit test checks that the two give
285	the same numbers on the golden fixture.
286	
287	The defender's path adds no score. Pass rates, framework coverage and the headline numbers are unchanged.
288	
289	## 7. Results
290	
291	### 7.1 Rows
292	
293	Every native row gains `Step` (a list, empty when the test names none). A family instance's row carries the
294	instance's value.
295	
296	### 7.2 `Steps` and `Goals`
297	
298	Two top-level properties. Like `Packs` and `Attachments`, they are written only when they have content (here,
299	when a row in the result names a step), so every other result stays as it is.
300	
301	```json
302	"Steps": [
303	  {
304	    "Id": "entra.ca-require-compliant-device",
305	    "Title": "Require a compliant device in Conditional Access",
306	    "Summary": "Sign-ins from devices Intune does not mark compliant are blocked.",
307	    "Product": "entra",
308	    "Goals": ["compliant-devices"],
309	    "Status": "NotDone",
310	    "Reason": null,
311	    "Readiness": "Blocked",
312	    "BlockedBy": ["intune.compliance-policies"],
313	    "Unconfirmed": ["intune.devices-compliant"],
314	    "Unlocks": [],
315	    "Rank": 9,
316	    "Tests": [
317	      { "Id": "MT.1001",   "Result": "Failed" },
318	      { "Id": "ZTA.24824", "Result": "NotRun", "ReasonCode": "NotInRun" }
319	    ],
320	    "Earlier": null,
321	    "Requires": ["intune.compliance-policies", "intune.devices-compliant", "entra.emergency-access-excluded", "entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts"],
322	    "RequiresOneOf": [],
323	    "RecommendedFirst": ["intune.mark-unassigned-noncompliant"],
324	    "Conflicts": [],
325	    "OnlyWhen": [],
326	    "Rollout": ["..."],
327	    "Sources": [{ "Url": "...", "Note": "...", "Reviewed": "2026-11-05" }]
328	  }
329	],
330	"Goals": [
331	  {
332	    "Id": "compliant-devices",
333	    "Title": "Require compliant devices",
334	    "Step": "entra.ca-require-compliant-device",
335	    "Steps": ["entra.emergency-access-excluded", "intune.compliance-policies", "..."],
336	    "Done": 3,
337	    "Applicable": 7,
338	    "Status": "InProgress"
339	  }
340	]
341	```
342	
343	- **Scope.** A step is in scope when a row that ran names it, or when it is a prerequisite, at any depth, of
344	  such a step. A goal is in scope when any of its steps is. A row ran when its result is anything but
345	  `NotRun`.
346	- **Tests come from the inventory, not only the rows.** `Tests` lists every test the engine knows that names
347	  the step: built-in tests from the catalog, custom tests that were discovered, and pack tests from each pack's
348	  catalogue. A test with no row has `Result` `NotRun` and `ReasonCode` `NotInRun`. The report can then name the
349	  command that checks it. This is how `Frameworks` already lists requirements that no row checks.
350	- **`Earlier`** is set on a step that is Not checked in this run when an earlier result in the output folder
351	  checked it: `{ "Status": "Done", "ExecutedAt": "...", "File": "..." }`. It is never mixed into this run's
352	  status or counts. `Get-MtPreviousResult` gains `LastKnown`, which is the newest earlier result for each test ID
353	  a step in scope names. It reads only files that `History` already lists, and only when some step in scope is
354	  Not checked. Today `Results` covers the newest earlier run only, and after a one-check run that run says
355	  little.
356	- **Goal status** is `Done` when every applicable step is Done, `NotStarted` when none is, and `InProgress`
357	  otherwise. When a step is Unknown or Not checked, the goal shows that count next to its progress.
358	- Built by `Get-MtResultStep` (internal, `powershell/internal/report/`) in `ConvertTo-MtMaesterResult`, next to
359	  `Get-MtResultFramework`. `Merge-MtPartitionResult` builds it again from the merged rows, as it does
360	  `Frameworks`, so that a multi-tenant or partitioned run is ordered as a whole.
361	- Additive, so the result schema moves from 2.1 to 2.2, and `website/docs/result-schema.md` documents both
362	  properties.
363	
364	### 7.3 Other outputs
365	
366	| Output | Change |
367	| --- | --- |
368	| CSV and Excel | `Step`, `Readiness` and `BlockedBy` columns on each test row |
369	| Markdown report | A "Do these first" list: the first five Ready steps, each with its failed tests. A one-line count of Blocked and Unconfirmed steps |
370	| JUnit XML | None |
371	| Console | One line in the run summary when `Steps` is present: `Defender's path: 3 ready · 2 blocked · 1 to check first` |
372	
373	## 8. Selection
374	
375	| Parameter | Config key | Selects |
376	| --- | --- | --- |
377	| `-Step` | `Selection.Step` | Tests whose `Step` matches. Takes a list, and `*` wildcards work (`intune.*`) |
378	| `-IncludePrerequisites` | `Selection.IncludePrerequisites` | Adds the verifying tests of every prerequisite of the steps that the selected tests name, at any depth |
379	
380	- They combine with the other selectors as in section 4 of the
381	  [test attributes design](./maester-3.0-test-attributes.md). `-IncludePrerequisites` is applied last, so
382	  `Invoke-Maester -TestId MT.1001 -IncludePrerequisites` runs MT.1001 and the checks of everything it depends on.
383	- Prerequisite tests that are Preview or LongRunning are included when `-IncludePrerequisites` reaches them,
384	  the same way an exact `-TestId` includes them. The ZTA family is the exception: it is included only when
385	  `-Suite ZTA` or `-IncludeLongRunning` is also given, because it runs the whole assessment. Its steps then show
386	  as Not checked with that command.
387	- `Get-MtTest -Step` filters the same way. There is no goal selector, because `-Step <goal step>
388	  -IncludePrerequisites` selects a whole goal. No new public command is added in Phase 1.
389	
390	## 9. Report
391	
392	Every view below is hidden when the result has no `Steps`, the same way views without data are hidden today.
393	
394	- **Action plan.** Opens with the defender's path: three groups of step cards in `Rank` order: Ready now, Check
395	  first and Blocked. A card shows the step, its failed tests, what it unlocks ("unlocks 2 steps, 6 failed
396	  checks"), its rollout and its sources. Below the groups, a lane for each goal in scope shows its steps in
397	  order with a status chip each. The existing ranked list of failed tests stays below that. A failed test whose
398	  step is Blocked moves after the tests that can be fixed now and shows "Blocked by …".
399	- **Test page.** When the test's step has prerequisites, a "Before you fix this" panel lists each one with its
400	  status and where that status came from: this run, an earlier run (with its date), or Not checked. It also gives
401	  the command that checks what is missing:
402	  `Invoke-Maester -TestId MT.1001 -IncludePrerequisites`. The How to fix tab adds the step's rollout.
403	- **Overview.** One card: Ready now, Blocked and Check first counts, with a link to the action plan.
404	- **Small runs.** With one to three tests that ran, there are no lanes. Each test page carries "Before you fix
405	  this" (section 10).
406	
407	The report reads `Steps` and `Goals` as written and works out nothing itself.
408	
409	## 10. Scoping rules
410	
411	The rule for every output: scope everything to what ran, and never infer a status for a test that did not run.
412	
413	| Run | Report | Console | Result |
414	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
415	| Full run | Groups and a lane for every goal in scope | The summary line | `Steps`, `Goals` |
416	| One suite or product | Only goals with a step in scope. A step whose tests were not selected shows "Not checked in this run" and the command to include them | The line, when a step is in scope | The steps in scope, with all their tests |
417	| One to three tests | No lanes. "Before you fix this" on each test page, with `Earlier` statuses and their dates | Nothing extra | The same |
418	| Tests that name no step (GitHub, Azure DevOps, Active Directory, most custom tests) | No change. The views stay hidden | No change | No `Steps` |
419	| A verifying test that could not run (service not connected, no licence) | The step is Unknown, with the reason and the fix command, and never Not done | Counted with the tests that did not run | `Status` `Unknown` with the reason codes |
420	
421	## 11. Readiness checks
422	
423	Seven steps in the first catalogue have no check. Two of them get readiness checks in Phase 1. Each check is a native
424	test in `tests/maester/<service>/`. It reads Graph through `powershell/internal/services/<service>/` helpers,
425	reports a count and a share, and lists the objects that hold the step back as affected objects. It passes when
426	the share is at least its `MinimumShare` parameter (an `int`, default `95`).
427	
428	| Step | Check | Reads | Notes |
429	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
430	| `intune.devices-compliant` | Devices that sign in are compliant | `devices` that signed in within 30 days, by `isManaged` and `isCompliant` | Lists the devices that would be blocked. Devices with no Entra identity can't be seen this way, which the result says |
431	| `entra.mfa-registered` | Enabled member users are registered for MFA | `reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` | Needs Entra ID P1. Excludes the emergency access accounts |
432	
433	Later: phishing-resistant method registration for all users (ZTA.21782 covers privileged users only),
434	password writeback once a Graph API reports it, security defaults being off in tenants licensed for
435	Conditional Access (section 15), and hybrid join and Windows device registration, which need sign-in data to
436	see the devices that have no identity yet. The Defender–Intune connector is partly covered already.
437	MT.1098 checks that Mobile Threat Defense connectors are healthy. Whether it fails when the Defender connector
438	is missing is confirmed in the expert pass.
439	
440	These are new MT checks. IDs are reserved on issue #697, and each goes through the duplicate review and the
441	attribute review in `AGENTS.md`. Their attribute values come from the rubric, not from this design.
442	
443	## 12. Object facts
444	
445	The Zero Trust facts work (`Add-MtAffectedObjectFact`, maester365/maester#2681) puts facts on
446	listed objects: join type, managed and compliant for devices, MFA and passwordless for users. They are the
447	drill-down behind a lane ("38 devices aren't managed"). They cannot replace readiness checks, because facts
448	attach only to objects the run lists and come from the Zero Trust export only when it ran. Readiness checks
449	write facts too.
450	
451	This design asked that work to give each fact a stable key and a raw value before the command ships, so that a
452	lane's drill-down never parses display text. It did, in maester365/maester#2681: a fact has `Name`, `Value`
453	(display text), `Tone`, an optional `Key` (dotted camelCase, `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\.[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)+$`), an
454	optional `Raw` (boolean, number, string, string list, or ISO 8601 UTC date), `Source` and `AsOf`. A fact with the
455	same `Key` from the same `Source` replaces the earlier one. The shared keys are listed under "Fact keys" in
456	`website/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results.md`. The ones this design reads:
457	
458	| Key | Raw | Used for |
459	| --- | --- | --- |
460	| `device.managed`, `device.compliant` | bool | The devices behind `intune.devices-compliant`. Management and compliance are separate facts |
461	| `device.joinType` | `AzureAd`, `ServerAd` or `Workplace` | Join coverage, for hybrid join and token protection |
462	| `device.os` | string | Which platforms need a compliance policy |
463	| `user.mfaRegistered`, `user.passwordless` | bool | The users behind `entra.mfa-registered` and the phishing-resistant steps |
464	| `user.privilegedRoles` | string list | The admins step of phishing-resistant MFA, and the privileged access goal |
465	| `signIn.daysSince` | int, or null when none is recorded | Leaving out stale devices and users. Counted from the fact's `AsOf`, not from now |
466	
467	User facts are recorded under both the object ID and the UPN, so a record has them whichever way it was keyed.
468	The readiness checks write the same keys for the objects they list.
469	
470	## 13. Keeping the catalogue current
471	
472	The sources are the nine Learn mirrors built with `merill/learn-mirror`. They crawl Learn four times a day and
473	make one commit per changed page. They cover Entra, Intune, Defender, security (Zero Trust), Purview, Teams,
474	SharePoint, Exchange and Windows Server. The tooling lives in `build/steps/`:
475	
476	| Script | Job |
477	| --- | --- |
478	| `Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1` | Clones or updates the mirrors into a cache folder, and builds a URL-to-file index. Old URLs are followed through Learn's redirects: 23 of the 77 Intune and Defender links in check guides are redirects today |
479	| `Find-MtStepCandidate.ps1` | For the Learn pages that check guides and catalogue sources link, pulls the prerequisite sections and sentences ("before you", "first", "must", "won't work without") with their file and line. Writes proposals as JSON for a maintainer, and optionally asks a model to reword them as `Note` text. Nothing enters the catalogue without review |
480	| `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` | For each source, lists the mirror commits to its file since `Reviewed`. Exits non-zero when any changed |
481	
482	A scheduled workflow, `.github/workflows/step-sources.yaml`, runs `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` weekly and keeps one
483	issue open that lists the steps whose sources changed, with the diff link for each. It opens issues, never pull
484	requests. A maintainer re-reads the page and bumps `Reviewed`.
485	
486	The unit tests make no network calls. They check that every `Url` is a well-formed Learn URL. Only the workflow
487	checks it against the mirrors.
488	
489	## 14. Enforcement
490	
491	`powershell/tests/general/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`:
492	
493	- every file matches the schema and has no unknown keys;
494	- step IDs are unique, their product key is in the taxonomy, and the file they are in is named after that key;
495	- every ID in `Requires`, `RequiresOneOf`, `RecommendedFirst`, `Conflicts` and a goal's `Step` exists;
496	- every `RequiresOneOf` group has at least two steps, and no step names the same step in two relationships;
497	- `Requires`, `RequiresOneOf` and `RecommendedFirst` together have no cycle, and the message names the cycle;
498	- every `OnlyWhen` key is a known condition;
499	- every step has a source, every `Note` is 200 characters or less, and maintainer-only sources are under 10%
500	  of all sources;
501	- every step belongs to at least one goal, and goal IDs are unique.
502	
503	`Get-MtStepProblem` makes these checks, plus two about the tests: every `Step` that a built-in test or a
504	`packs/*/taxonomy.json` names exists, and (with `-Coverage`, over every built-in test) `Unchecked` is set exactly
505	on the steps that no test names. `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` fails on all of them except the `Unchecked`
506	check, because the build can run on a folder that holds only some of the tests. A run only warns about a step
507	the catalogue does not have.
508	
509	## 15. The first catalogue
510	
511	This is a draft from the research, and Phase 1's expert pass (milestone M2) confirms every row against the
512	mirrors before any test is tagged. Three goals were checked against Learn: compliant devices, risk policies
513	and token protection. The other four come from known Microsoft guidance and still need the same check.
514	
515	| Goal | Steps, in order | Verifying tests (draft) |
516	| --- | --- | --- |
517	| Foundation (under most goals) | `entra.emergency-access-excluded` · `entra.ca-exclude-sync-accounts` (only when `hybrid-identity`) | MT.1005, MT.1034 · MT.1020 |
518	| `compliant-devices` Require compliant devices | `intune.compliance-policies` → `intune.automatic-enrollment` (recommended first) → `intune.devices-compliant` → `intune.mark-unassigned-noncompliant` (recommended first) → `entra.ca-require-compliant-device`. `entra.ca-require-managed-device` needs one of `intune.devices-compliant` and `entra.hybrid-join` | ZTA.24541–24543, ZTA.24545, ZTA.24547 · ZTA.24546 · new check · MT.1054, CIS.M365.4.1 · MT.1001, ZTA.24824 · CIS.M365.5.2.2.9, CISA.MS.AAD.3.7, MT.1014 |
519	| `risk-policies` Risk-based Conditional Access | `entra.mfa-registered` → `entra.password-hash-sync` (only when hybrid, recommended first) → `entra.password-writeback` (only when hybrid) → `entra.remediate-risky-users` (recommended first) → `entra.ca-user-risk` and `entra.ca-sign-in-risk` → `entra.ca-risk-policies-separate` | new check · CIS.M365.5.1.8.1 · unchecked · MT.1260 · MT.1013, CIS.M365.5.2.2.6, CISA.MS.AAD.2.1 and MT.1012, CIS.M365.5.2.2.7, CISA.MS.AAD.2.3 · MT.1049 |
520	| `phishing-resistant-mfa` Phishing-resistant MFA | `entra.passkeys-enabled` and `entra.temporary-access-pass` → `entra.windows-hello` → `entra.phishing-resistant-registered` → `entra.phishing-resistant-admins` → `entra.phishing-resistant-all` | EIDSCA.AF01–AF06, ZTA.21839 · EIDSCA.AT01, AT02 · ZTA.24551 · ZTA.21782 (admins only) · CISA.MS.AAD.3.6, ZTA.21783, ZTA.21781 · CISA.MS.AAD.3.1, ASD.ISM-1872, ZTA.21784 |
521	| `privileged-access` Standing privilege to PIM | `entra.emergency-access-excluded` → `entra.pim-eligible-roles` → `entra.pim-alerts` → `entra.pim-roles-used` | MT.1025–MT.1028, MT.1031, ZTA.21816, ZTA.21876 · CISA.MS.AAD.7.7 · MT.1030 |
522	| `token-protection` Token protection | `entra.windows-devices-registered` → `entra.ca-token-protection` (rollout: report-only pilot) | unchecked: needs sign-in logs to see Windows sign-ins without a device identity · CIS.M365.5.2.2.16, ZTA.21941, ZTA.21786 |
523	| `email-authentication` Email authentication | `exchange.spf` and `exchange.dkim` → `exchange.dmarc-monitor` → `exchange.dmarc-enforce` | CIS.M365.2.1.8, CISA.MS.EXO.2.2, ORCA.235 · CIS.M365.2.1.9, CISA.MS.EXO.3.1, ORCA.108, ORCA.108.1 · CIS.M365.2.1.10, CISA.MS.EXO.4.1, 4.3 · CISA.MS.EXO.4.2, MT.1182 |
524	| `defender-device-risk` Defender risk in compliance | `defender.endpoint-onboarding` → `intune.defender-connector` → `intune.compliance-device-risk` (requires `intune.compliance-policies`) | ZTA.41045 · MT.1098, ZTA.24871 · MT.1216, MT.1231, MT.1235 |
525	
526	That is 34 steps over about 75 existing tests, plus the two new checks. Expect most tests to name no step:
527	antivirus settings, sharing
528	settings and most EIDSCA values stand on their own. The value is concentrated where Conditional Access,
529	devices and authentication meet.
530	
531	The first catalogue has no `Conflicts` entry yet. The obvious one is that Conditional Access policies need
532	security defaults turned off. MT.1021 can't verify it, because it checks that security defaults are on and
533	skips any tenant with Entra ID P1 or better, which is every tenant that uses Conditional Access. A readiness
534	check, "Security defaults are off where Conditional Access is licensed", would make the conflict checkable.
535	It is listed with the later checks in section 11.
536	
537	Candidates for later goals come from the research: legacy authentication,
538	guest access, app consent, workload credentials, hybrid hardening, SSPR, LAPS, data protection, SharePoint
539	sharing, audit, Defender for Office 365, Global Secure Access, AI agents, Copilot readiness, Insider Risk,
540	Defender for Cloud Apps, third-party mail filters, Defender for Identity, Power Platform and Active Directory.
541	
542	## 16. Delivery
543	
544	| Milestone | Work | Needs |
545	| --- | --- | --- |
546	| M1 Format | Schema and loader (`Get-MtStepCatalog`, internal), the `Step` attribute in C#, the schema table and the reader, `StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`, and the compliant-devices goal as the fixture | This design |
547	| M2 Catalogue | Expert pass on the seven goals against the mirrors, then `Step` on about 75 tests, plus `Step` in the Zero Trust `taxonomy.json` | M1, and the instance-attribute change on `feat/zta-taxonomy-mapping` |
548	| M3 Engine | `Step` on rows, `Get-MtResultStep` (status, readiness, rank, scope), `LastKnown`, `-Step`, `-IncludePrerequisites`, `Get-MtTest -Step`, CSV and Markdown columns, the console line | M1 |
549	| M4 Report | Action plan groups and lanes, Before you fix this, rollout in How to fix, the overview card | M3's result shape. It can start on sample data once section 7 is final |
550	| M5 Readiness checks | The two checks of section 11 | M1 for `Step`. The checks can be written before it |
551	| M6 Tooling | `build/steps/` scripts and the weekly workflow | M1 |
552	| M7 Docs and site | `Step` in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`, a defender's path page, and one page per goal on maester.dev built by `prepare-data.mjs` | M2 |
553	
554	Once M1 lands, M2, M5 and M6 touch different files and can run in parallel sessions. M3 and M4 follow in order.
555	
556	## 17. Decisions
557	
558	The owner accepted the recommended answer to each decision on 5 November 2026.
559	
560	| # | Decision | Ruling | Alternatives considered |
561	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
562	| 1 | Name readers see | **Defender's path**, the counterpart of an attack path | "Implementation order", "Do this first" |
563	| 2 | Attribute name | **`Step`** | `Change` (clashes with the report's Changes page and with drift), `Prerequisite` (says the opposite of what most tests are) |
564	| 3 | What a lane is called | **Goal** (`Goals` in the result) | "Path", which clashes with `-Path` on `Invoke-Maester` and `Get-MtTest` and with file paths in the result |
565	| 4 | Where the catalogue lives | **`powershell/assets/steps/`**, beside the taxonomy, with no build change | A top-level `steps/` folder like `packs/`, which is easier to find but needs a build copy and a layout rule. Not under `tests/`, which holds only suites |
566	| 5 | Statuses | **Done, Not done, Unknown, Not checked, Not applicable** | Only Done and Not done, which turns every gap into a failure |
567	| 6 | Investigate | **Counts as Unknown** | Counts as Not done |
568	| 7 | Conflicts | **Block** while the conflicting step is on, declared on the step that needs the other off | Warn only |
569	| 8 | Selectors | **`-Step` and `-IncludePrerequisites`**, no goal selector, no new public command | A `Get-MtStep` command, which would add public API to keep |
570	| 9 | Packs and custom tests | **May name built-in steps.** Their own catalogues come later | Built-in tests only |
571	| 10 | Readiness thresholds | **A `MinimumShare` parameter, default 95** | A fixed threshold. A config key shared by all the readiness checks |
572	| 11 | Earlier statuses | **`LastKnown` per test, read only when a step in scope is Not checked** | The newest earlier run only, which says little after a one-check run |
573	| 12 | Catalogue wording | **Maester's own words and a link, 200 characters at most** | Quoting Learn |
574	| 13 | Mining output | **Proposals for review, and a weekly issue for changed sources** | A workflow that opens pull requests |
575	| 14 | Fact keys | **Ask the facts work for `Key` and a raw value before it ships** | Add them later. That breaks nothing, but costs more |
576	| 15 | Action plan | **The defender's path leads the page, with the ranked list below** | A separate page, which keeps today's plan unchanged but hides the strong point |
577	
578	## 18. Not in this design
579	
580	- The insights step (`Insight.<ID>.ps1`), attack scenarios, the most exposed identities and the reader profile.
581	  They are the rest of Phase 1 and get a design of their own. Steps are the same unit as the planned "fix once,
582	  close many" groups, so that work reuses this catalogue.
583	- Custom step catalogues for users and packs.
584	- Measured user impact from sign-in logs and report-only results. It would feed readiness later.
585	- Goals for GitHub, Azure DevOps and Active Directory. Until they exist, those runs look as they do today.
586	- A model that decides pass, fail, severity or order. Order comes from the catalogue, and every relationship
587	  cites its source.
588

# Brief for the defender's path research agents (milestone M2)

You are doing research only. Do NOT edit, create or delete any file in the repository
(`/Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/defenders-path-m2-8b8ecc`). Write your findings only to the file
named in your prompt, under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill-github-maester--claude-worktrees-defenders-path-m2-8b8ecc/f8bda74f-6c1f-4f6d-9546-cf4020f4c33b/scratchpad/research/`.

## Context

Maester is a PowerShell framework that checks Microsoft 365 security configuration. The defender's path orders
fixes the way Microsoft Learn documents them: what must be in place first, what a fix unlocks, and whether the
tenant is ready. Read these in the repository first:

- `docs/proposals/defenders-path.md`, sections 3, 4 (format, relationships, conditions, sources and wording),
  5 (the `Step` attribute, and the rule that tests with different definitions of done get different steps) and 15
  (the DRAFT table you are checking).
- `powershell/assets/steps/entra.json` and `intune.json`: the M1 steps, as an example of the finished format.

Key rules:

- A step is one change ("Require X in Conditional Access", imperative) or one tenant state ("Devices that sign in
  are compliant", a statement). ID `<product-key>.<kebab-name>`; product keys: `entra`, `intune`, `exchange`,
  `defender`.
- Relationships: `Requires` (must be done first, or the change fails or locks users out), `RequiresOneOf` (groups
  of 2+, any one will do), `RecommendedFirst` (safer or more useful first; never blocks), `Conflicts` (must be off
  first), `OnlyWhen` (`hybrid-identity` or `license:<service plan>`, e.g. `license:AAD_PREMIUM_P2`).
- Every relationship must be backed by a Microsoft Learn page. If Learn does not back a draft relationship, say so
  and recommend dropping it. Do not invent relationships from general knowledge.
- Section 15 is a draft. Change steps, order or relationships where Learn says otherwise.
- Tests whose definition of done differs (stricter, narrower, a different setting) need separate steps. Example
  from section 5: CIS 5.2.2.9 accepts compliant OR hybrid joined devices, MT.1001 needs compliance, so they name
  different steps. A test scoped to admins only does not prove a step about all users.
- A shim is a test whose body is `return <another test's function>`; it must name the same step as the test it
  calls.
- EIDSCA (`tests/eidsca/`) and ORCA (`tests/orca/`) tests are generated; just report whether they verify a step.
- Zero Trust Assessment tests (ZTA.xxxxx) live in the pack; `packs/zero-trust-assessment/catalog.json` has their
  titles. They cannot carry `Step` yet, so a step that only ZTA tests check stays "Unchecked" naming the ZTA IDs.
  Confirm each draft ZTA ID's title matches the step.

## Learn sources

Shallow clones of the Learn mirrors are at
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill-github-maester--claude-worktrees-defenders-path-m2-8b8ecc/f8bda74f-6c1f-4f6d-9546-cf4020f4c33b/scratchpad/mirrors/`:

result.output:
- Sign-in risk policy

Warning

Don't combine sign-in risk and user risk conditions in the same Conditional Access policy. Create separate policies for each risk condition.

![Screenshot of a Conditional Access policy showing risk as conditions.](media/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies/sign-in-risk-conditions.png)

## Prerequisites
----
### Risk remediation

Organizations can choose to block access when risk is detected. Blocking sometimes stops legitimate users from doing what they need to. A better solution is to configure user and sign-in risk-based Conditional Access policies that [allow users to self-remediate](howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock#end-user-self-remediation).

Warning

Users must register for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication before they face a situation requiring remediation. For hybrid users that are synced from on-premises, password writeback must be enabled. Users not registered are blocked and require administrator intervention.

Password change (I know my password and want to change it to something new) outside of the risky user policy remediation flow doesn't meet the requirement for secure password change.

### Microsoft recommendations

Microsoft recommends the following risk policy configurations to protect your organization:

### User risk policy

Organizations should select **Require risk remediation** when user risk level is **High**. For passwordless users, Microsoft Entra revokes the user's sessions so they must reauthenticate. For users with passwords, they're prompted to complete a secure password change after a successful Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication.

When **Require risk remediation** is selected, two settings are automatically applied:

- **Require authentication strength** is automatically selected as a grant control.
- **Sign-in frequency - Every time** is automatically applied as a session control.

### Sign-in risk policy

Require Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication when sign-in risk level is **Medium** or **High**. This configuration allows users to prove it's them by using one of their registered authentication methods, remediating the sign-in risk.

We also recommend including the [sign-in frequency session control](../identity/conditional-access/concept-session-lifetime#require-reauthentication-every-time) to require reauthentication for risky sign-ins. A successful "strong authentication" usually via multifactor authentication or passwordless authentication, is the only way to self-remediate sign-in risk, regardless of the risk level.

## Enable policies

Organizations can choose to deploy risk-based policies in Conditional Access using the following steps or use [Conditional Access templates](../identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policy-common).

Before organizations enable these policies, they should take action to [investigate](howto-identity-protection-investigate-risk) and [remediate](howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock) any active risks.

----

Organizations can deploy this policy by following the steps outlined below or by using the [Conditional Access templates](concept-conditional-access-policy-common).

## Require risk remediation

This risk remediation policy covers both password-based and passwordless users.

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator).
2. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access**.
3. Select **New policy**.
4. Give your policy a name. We recommend that organizations create a meaningful standard for the names of their policies.
5. Under **Assignments**, select **Users or workload identities**.
    1. Under **Include**, select **All users**.
    2. Under **Exclude**, select **Users and groups** and choose your organization's emergency access or break-glass accounts.
    3. Select **Done**.
6. Under **Target resources** > **Include**, select **All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps')**.
7. Under **Conditions** > **User risk**, set **Configure** to **Yes**.
    1. Under **Configure user risk levels needed for policy to be enforced**, select **High**. [This guidance is based on Microsoft recommendations and might be different for each organization](../../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies#choosing-acceptable-risk-levels)
    2. Select **Done**.
8. Under **Access controls** > **Grant**, select **Grant access**.
    1. Select **Require risk remediation**. The **Require authentication strength** grant control is automatically selected. Choose the strength appropriate for your organization.
    2. Select **Select**.
9. Under **Session**, **Sign-in frequency - Every time** is automatically applied as a session control and is mandatory.
10. Confirm your settings and set **Enable policy** to **Report-only**.
11. Select **Create** to create your policy.

After confirming your settings using [policy impact or report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only#reviewing-results), move the **Enable policy** toggle from **Report-only** to **On**.---
## User risk-based Conditional Access policy

ID Protection analyzes signals about user accounts and calculates a risk score based on the probability that the user is compromised. If a user has risky user sign-in behavior, or their credentials were leaked, ID Protection uses these signals to calculate the user risk level. Administrators can configure risk-based Conditional Access policies to enforce access controls based on user risk, including requirements such as:

1. Require risk remediation: ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow for all authentication methods.
2. Require password change: ID Protection blocks access until user completes a secure password change.
3. Block access: ID Protection blocks the user until risk is addressed.

Policies requiring either #1 or #2 forces end users to remediate their user risk and unblock themselves.

## Require risk remediation control

This control uses adaptive risk remediation to let you author a Conditional Access risk policy that accommodates all authentication methods, including password-based and passwordless. This means that when you select "Require risk remediation" in your policy's grant controls, Microsoft Entra ID Protection manages the appropriate remediation flow based on the threat observed and the user's authentication method. For detailed steps on how to enable adaptive risk remediation, see [Configure risk policies](howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies#microsoft-recommendations).

- **Password authentication**: Risky user has an active risk detection, such as a leaked credential, password spray, or session history involving a compromised password. The user is prompted to perform a secure password change and when completed, their previous sessions are revoked.
- **Passwordless authentication**: Risky user has an active risk detection, but it doesn't involve a compromised password. Possible risk detections include anomalous token, impossible travel, or unfamiliar sign-in properties. The user's sessions are revoked and they're prompted to sign in again.
- **Attacker-added device**: Risky user is flagged by Microsoft's threat intelligence as having a device added by an attacker. The Entra device object is disabled, blocking new token issuance. The user's sessions are revoked, and they're prompted to sign-in again.

#### Special considerations

- **Require Risk Remediation** remediates user risk, not sign-in risk.
- If a user is assigned to multiple policies, precedence applies: **Require risk remediation** overrides **Require password change**, and **Block** overrides all others. To avoid conflicts, assign each user to only one of these policies at a time.
- **Require authentication strength** and **Sign-in frequency - Every time** are automatically applied to the policy to ensure that after session revocation, end users are immediately prompted to reauthenticate with the specified authentication strength.

20	## Answers to the brief's questions
21	
22	1. **Learn's order.** Enable methods (DEPLOY 144-147 "must be turned on", 166-173; PASSKEY 49, 66-72) → bootstrap with existing MFA or a TAP (TAP 47-50; DEPLOY 108, 121, 125-127) → users register a portable credential first, then local ones (DEPLOY 95-98, 129, 151-153) → measure, then enforce with an authentication strength (DEPLOY 186, 250, 346-357), admins first "typically" (DEPLOY 202, 352-357). Hard Requires: registration before enforcement (CA-ADMIN 48-50 warns of tenant lockout; HOWITWORKS 109, 113 says users not registered can't reach the resource), emergency access exclusion (CA-ADMIN 87-90, 114; DEPLOY 256). RecommendedFirst: TAP (one of two bootstrap paths), admins before everyone (Learn says "typically ... may change", DEPLOY 202), passkeys before Windows Hello (portable credential first, DEPLOY 129, 153).
23	2. **Windows Hello for Business is one method among several, not a prerequisite.** The built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength accepts WHfB *or* platform credential, FIDO2 and multifactor CBA (STRENGTHS 72-76, 86-90). DEPLOY lists WHfB as a recommended *local* credential beside Entra passkey on Windows and CBA (163-164) and never puts it on the enforcement path (350-399). Model it as a member of a `RequiresOneOf` group, not a link in the chain.
24	3. **EIDSCA.** AF01 (state) and AF02 (self-service setup) define "passkeys enabled"; AF03-AF06 are hardening values Learn makes optional. AT01 (state) defines "TAP enabled"; AT02 (one-time) is hardening that Learn does not require. Details per step.
25	4. **Benchmarks.** CISA.MS.AAD.3.1 = all users; ASD.ISM-1872 is a shim of it. CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 and CIS.M365.5.2.2.5 = admin roles only, with different role lists. CISA 3.1 accepts phishing-resistant only; the "or alternative MFA" path is CISA.MS.AAD.3.2, which skips when 3.1 passes (`tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.2.ps1`) and belongs to an MFA step, not this goal. No MT test checks phishing-resistant strength (MT.1006/MT.1007 accept any MFA).
26	5. **ZTA.** 21839, 24551, 21782, 21783 match their steps. 21781 and 21784 do not (see step 8 and 9). Extra IDs found: 21838, 21840, 21845, 21846, 21801, 24568.
27	6. **Admin registration before admin enforcement** is Learn-backed and is a hard Requires (CA-ADMIN 48-50). **All-user registration** is backed too (DEPLOY 95, 250; HOWITWORKS 113) and needs its own step, Unchecked until the section 11 readiness check exists (ZTA.21801 checks it).

48	## Steps, in order
49	
50	### 1. `defender.spf`: Publish an SPF record for every domain that sends mail
51	Summary: Receiving servers can check that mail from your domains comes from Microsoft 365 or another sender you list.
52	- Relationships: none.
53	- Source (definition): SPF lines 60-63, 112-144, 154-173, parked 73 and 174-193. Note: "Each custom domain and sending
54	  subdomain needs one SPF TXT record naming Microsoft 365 and any other senders. onmicrosoft.com is covered; parked
55	  domains get v=spf1 -all." (169 chars)
56	- Rollout (ABOUT lines 283-298; SPF lines 144, 218-229):
57	  1. List every system that sends as the domain: Microsoft 365, on-premises servers and third-party services.
58	  2. Publish one SPF TXT record per sending domain and subdomain, and keep it under ten DNS lookups.
59	  3. Give domains that never send mail the record v=spf1 -all.
60	- Tests:
61	  - CIS.M365.2.1.8 (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.2.1.8.ps1` 37-118). Every custom accepted domain (the initial and
62	    coexistence domains are excluded; parked domains are included) has an SPF record whose `all` term, after any
63	    redirect, is `-all` or `~all`. **Matches.**
64	  - CISA.MS.EXO.2.2 (`tests/cisa/exchange/Test.CISA.MS.EXO.2.2.ps1` 37-89). Every domain with sending enabled,
65	    including the initial domain, has an SPF record whose includes, nested ones too, contain
66	    `spf.protection.outlook.com` or `outlook.com`. It does not check the `all` qualifier. **Shares the step, but checks
67	    a different part of the record.** This is CISA v1 logic. The current upstream text, MS.EXO.2.2v3, is "...fails
68	    all non-approved senders" and accepts either -all or ~all (ScubaGear `baselines/exo.md` lines 132-142). That is
69	    exactly what CIS 2.1.8 checks, so the CISA test should become a shim of `Test-MtCisSpfRecordsPublished`
70	    (AGENTS.md duplicate rule). It probably also fails GCC High, DoD and 21Vianet tenants, whose include is
71	    `spf.protection.office365.us` or `.partner.outlook.cn` (SPF lines 163-172). Verify this before relying on it.
72	
73	### 2. `defender.spf-hard-fail` (new): End every SPF record with -all
74	Summary: Receivers are told to reject mail from servers the SPF record does not list, so DMARC can act on unsigned spoofed mail.
75	- RecommendedFirst `defender.spf`: ABOUT lines 283-298. Start with the senders you know and ~all, find the rest,
76	  then switch to -all. Note: "Publish the known senders with ~all first and add the rest as you find them. A hard
77	  fail before then would bounce mail from a sender you missed." (144 chars)
78	- RecommendedFirst `defender.dmarc-published`: SPF lines 76-78 and 130-134. DMARC reports are the main way to find
79	  sources and SPF failures, and in complex organizations a p=none DMARC record should go in early. Note: "DMARC
80	  aggregate reports reveal which servers send as the domain, so read them before -all rejects a source nobody
81	  listed." (121 chars)
82	- Rollout:
83	  1. Keep ~all until the DMARC aggregate reports show no legitimate source failing SPF.
84	  2. Change the qualifier to -all one domain at a time, keeping one SPF record per domain.
85	- Tests: ORCA.235 (generated; `powershell/internal/generated/orca/check-ORCA235.ps1` 72-165). Every accepted domain
86	  that has an MX record, onmicrosoft.com included, has exactly one SPF record, and it uses `-all`. A `~all` record,
87	  no qualifier, or two records fail. **Matches** (stricter than CIS 2.1.8, which is why this is a separate step).
88	
89	### 3. `defender.dkim`: Sign outbound mail with DKIM for every custom domain
90	Summary: Mail from your custom domains carries a DKIM signature that aligns with the From domain, survives forwarding and passes DMARC.
91	- Relationships: none. GUIDE line 92 lists SPF, DKIM and DMARC "in that order". The troubleshooting page
92	  (`email-authentication-troubleshoot.md` line 177) fixes SPF first because a DNS-only change is fastest. Neither page
93	  says that DKIM depends on SPF, so I added no edge.
94	- Source (definition): DKIM lines 81-90 (onmicrosoft.com is signed automatically; custom domains are not signed
95	  until you configure them), 99 (parked domains get no DKIM), 185-243 and 345-369 (add the domain, create both CNAMEs,
96	  then turn signing on; the toggle fails while the CNAMEs are missing), 634-648 (both selectors are needed). Note:
97	  "Custom domains aren't signed until both selector CNAMEs exist and signing is on. onmicrosoft.com is signed
98	  already, and parked domains get no DKIM records." (148 chars)
99	- Rollout:
100	  1. Read the two CNAME values for the domain from the Defender portal or `Get-DkimSigningConfig`.
101	  2. Create both selector CNAME records at the DNS host and wait until Microsoft 365 detects them.
102	  3. Turn on DKIM signing for the domain and confirm that its status shows it is signing.
103	- Tests (all **match**; they scope domains slightly differently):
104	  - CIS.M365.2.1.9 (`tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.2.1.9.ps1` 52-141). Every accepted domain except the initial,
105	    coexistence and parked (`SendingFromDomainDisabled`) domains has a DkimSigningConfig that is Enabled with Status

108	    check. It covers the initial domain: that domain passes when it has no config. If it has a disabled config the

110	  - ORCA.108 (generated; `check-ORCA108.ps1`). Every custom domain that has an MX record has DKIM signing enabled.
111	  - ORCA.108.1 (generated; `check-ORCA108_1.ps1`). For those domains with signing enabled, both the selector1 and
112	    selector2 CNAMEs resolve to the values Exchange expects.
113	  - Not shims. CIS 2.1.9 and CISA 3.1 are almost the same code. They are a candidate for one test and a shim with a
114	    parameter (out of scope for M2).

param()

    Write-Verbose 'Getting named locations...'
    $locations = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'identity/conditionalAccess/namedLocations'
    $ipLocations = @($locations | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.ipNamedLocation' })

    $report = foreach ($location in $ipLocations) {
        $rangeCount = @($location.ipRanges).Count
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Name = $location.displayName
            Ranges = $rangeCount
            Trusted = [bool]$location.isTrusted
            Pass = $rangeCount -gt 0 -and $location.isTrusted -eq $true
        }
    }
    $testResult = @($report | Where-Object { $_.Pass }).Count -gt 0

    $passText = 'At least one trusted IP named location with IP ranges is defined.'
    $failText = if ($ipLocations.Count -eq 0) { 'No IP named locations are defined.' } else { 'No IP named location is both trusted and has IP ranges.' }

    $resultMd = "| Named location | IP ranges | Trusted | Result |`n"
    $resultMd += "| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
-----
    param()

    Write-Verbose 'Getting Conditional Access policies...'
    $policies = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy
    $phishingResistantMethods = @('windowsHelloForBusiness', 'fido2', 'x509CertificateMultiFactor')

    $candidates = @($policies | Where-Object { $_.grantControls.authenticationStrength.id -and (@($_.conditions.signInRiskLevels).Count -eq 0 -and @($_.conditions.userRiskLevels).Count -eq 0) })

    $report = foreach ($policy in $candidates) {
        $problems = @(Get-MtCisConditionalAccessScopeProblem -Policy $policy -Users AdministratorRoles)
        $grantProblems = @(Get-MtCisConditionalAccessGrantProblem -Policy $policy)
        $excludedApplications = @($policy.conditions.applications.excludeApplications | Where-Object { $_ })
        $allowed = @($policy.grantControls.authenticationStrength.allowedCombinations)
        $otherMethods = @($allowed | Where-Object { $phishingResistantMethods -notcontains $_ })
        $checks = [ordered]@{
            'Scope covers the required users and apps' = $problems.Count -eq 0
            'No excluded applications' = $excludedApplications.Count -eq 0
            'Phishing-resistant strength only' = $allowed.Count -gt 0 -and $otherMethods.Count -eq 0
            'Grant controls combine as required' = $grantProblems.Count -eq 0
            'Enabled' = $policy.state -eq 'enabled'
        }
        $failed = @($checks.GetEnumerator() | Where-Object { -not $_.Value } | ForEach-Object { $_.Key })
        $details = @($problems) + @($grantProblems)
        $failedText = $failed -join ', '
        if ($details.Count -gt 0) { $failedText += " ($($details -join '; '))" }
        $excludedApplicationsText = if ($excludedApplications.Count -gt 0) { $excludedApplications -join ', ' } else { 'None' }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $policy.displayName; State = $policy.state; ExcludedApplications = $excludedApplicationsText; Failed = $failedText; Pass = $failed.Count -eq 0 }
    }
    $testResult = @($report | Where-Object { $_.Pass }).Count -gt 0
    $passText = 'An enabled Conditional Access policy requires phishing-resistant MFA for the administrative roles.'
    $failText = if ($candidates.Count -eq 0) { 'No Conditional Access policy that uses an authentication strength was found.' } else { 'No enabled Conditional Access policy requires phishing-resistant MFA for all the administrative roles.' }

import re
def add_step(path, key_regex, step, indent):
    s = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(key_regex, s)
    assert m, key_regex
    # find the closing brace of this object: the first line at the object's indent that is '}' or '},'
    start = m.end()
    close = re.compile(r'\n' + re.escape(indent[:-2]) + r'\}', re.M)
    c = close.search(s, start)
    assert c
    body = s[start:c.start()]
    assert '"Step"' not in body
    new = body.rstrip() + ',\n' + indent + '"Step": [\n' + indent + '  "' + step + '"\n' + indent + ']'
    s = s[:start] + new + s[c.start():]
    open(path, 'w').write(s)

### Changes from the draft

- **A new goal, `managed-devices`.** A compliant or hybrid joined device is something Learn offers organizations
  that aren't ready to require compliance for everyone (policy-all-users-device-compliance). It is another end
  state, not a step towards compliant devices. It is also what CIS 5.2.2.9 and CISA 3.7 ask for. MT.1014 covers
  admin roles only, so it gets its own step, `entra.ca-require-managed-device-admins`. Learn offers the admin
  policy first, so that step is recommended first. `entra.hybrid-join` is new and Unchecked. Graph shows which
  devices are hybrid joined, but not the domain PCs that aren't.
- **Foundation.** `entra.emergency-access-accounts` is new. Learn's prerequisite for PIM is that the accounts
  exist and keep Global Administrator as a permanent active assignment (security-emergency-access,
  pim-deployment-plan). That is a different fact from their Conditional Access exclusion. The same page creates
  the accounts before it excludes them, so the new step is recommended before `entra.emergency-access-excluded`.
- **Risk policies.**
  - Password writeback is required only for the user-risk policy. Sign-in risk is cleared with MFA
    (howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies).
  - Password hash sync and remediating existing high-risk users are recommended before the user-risk policy. Learn
    puts the review first in its deployment plan (how-to-deploy-identity-protection) and ties leaked-credential
    detection to password hash sync (id-protection-faq).
  - The goal ends at `entra.ca-user-risk`, with the sign-in risk policy recommended first. Unremediated sign-in risk
    raises user risk (howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock).
  - Learn's rule that the two risk conditions go in separate policies is a warning, not an order. It is now in both
    steps' rollout, so `entra.ca-risk-policies-separate` and MT.1049 left the catalogue.
  - `entra.trusted-named-locations` (CIS 5.2.2.14) is new and recommended before sign-in risk. Some detections use
    trusted locations to cut false positives.
  - `entra.ca-user-risk` is `Unchecked`. Learn now recommends the Require risk remediation grant (policy-risk-based-user),
    and MT.1013 and CIS 5.2.2.6 accept only Require password change.
- **Phishing-resistant MFA.**
  - Windows Hello for Business is one of the methods that meet the phishing-resistant strength, not a link in the
    chain (concept-authentication-strengths). It is now `intune.windows-hello`, in a "one of" group with passkeys,
    certificate-based authentication and macOS Platform SSO. A tenant that uses only one of them is not blocked.
  - Registration is split into admins and all users, and enforcement requires each. Learn warns that an
    unregistered admin can lock the tenant out (policy-admin-phish-resistant-mfa).
  - The Temporary Access Pass is one of two ways to bootstrap registration, so it is recommended first, not
    required.
  - Admins come first "typically", so the admin policy is recommended before the all-users one, not required.
- **Privileged access.**
  - The draft's `entra.pim-alerts` became `entra.pim-notifications`. CISA 7.7 checks notification recipients, not
    PIM security alerts.
  - `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` (CIS 5.3.4, CISA 7.6) is new. It requires the emergency access accounts,
    because approval with no available approver locks the tenant (pim-how-to-change-default-settings).
  - Learn sets role settings before it hands out eligible assignments (pim-getting-started), so both settings steps
    are recommended first.
  - `entra.pim-roles-used` (MT.1030) left the goal. Learn treats unused roles as an alert to act on and access
    reviews as the prevention, not as a rollout step.
- **Token protection.** The step is `entra.ca-token-protection-windows`, because every test checks a Windows
  policy and Learn deploys Apple separately with its own prerequisites. Device registration is recommended first,
  not required: current Windows builds prompt unregistered users to register (deployment-guide-token-protection-windows).
  The same guide pairs the policy with blocking unknown platforms, which MT.1015 checks.
- **Email authentication.**
  - The steps are `defender.*`. Learn documents them under Defender for Office 365, DKIM is set up in the Defender
    portal, and most of the tests declare `defender`.
  - SPF and DKIM are required only by the steps that enforce DMARC. A p=none record changes no delivery, and Learn
    advises publishing one early to find senders (email-authentication-spf-configure).
  - `dmarc-monitor` became `defender.dmarc-published` (CISA 4.1).
  - CIS 2.1.10 rejects p=none, so it verifies `defender.dmarc-enforce`, which means quarantine or reject with
    reports on every domain, as the deployment guide asks (mdo-deployment-guide).
  - The goal ends at p=reject (`defender.dmarc-reject`, CISA 4.2 and MT.1182).
  - ORCA.235 fails `~all`, so it verifies its own step, `defender.spf-hard-fail`.
- **Defender device risk.**
  - Learn connects the services before it onboards devices, so the draft order is reversed.
  - The connector's per-platform compliance toggle is a step of its own (configure-integration).
  - Compliance policies are recommended first, not required, because the risk score is one setting inside them.
  - MT.1098 doesn't verify the connector (section 11). MT.1235 reads the third-party threat level on Android
    device administrator, not Defender's risk score. MT.1216 reads a macOS setting that Learn doesn't document.
    Only MT.1231 (iOS) verifies the step.

| Tests | Why |
| --- | --- |
| MT.1013, CIS.M365.5.2.2.6 | Reject Learn's Require risk remediation grant. They name `entra.ca-user-risk` once they accept it, which needs `Prefer: include-unknown-enum-members` on the policy request |
| CISA.MS.AAD.2.1, CISA.MS.AAD.2.3, CIS.M365.5.2.2.8 | Block risky users or sign-ins. Learn prefers self-remediation and treats a block as a stopgap |
| MT.1049 | Its rule moved into the risk steps' rollout |
| CISA.MS.AAD.3.6 | Covers a different set of admin roles from CIS 5.2.2.5 and Learn, so the two would disagree in one run |
| EIDSCA.AF03–AF06, EIDSCA.AT02 | Hardening that Learn makes optional |
| MT.1025–MT.1028, MT.1030, CISA.MS.AAD.7.4 | Admin-account hygiene, not eligibility. CISA 7.4 also fails the permanent emergency access accounts that Learn asks for |
| CISA.MS.EXO.4.3 | Applies only to CISA's own reporting address |
| MT.1098, MT.1216, MT.1235 | See "Defender device risk" above |

- MT.1001 accepts any enabled policy that uses the compliant-device control.
- CISA 3.7 fails a stricter policy that requires compliance only.
- MT.1231 fails a tenant with no iOS compliance policy.
- CISA 7.5 fails emergency access assignments made outside PIM.

- third-party mail filters, Defender for Identity, Power Platform and Active Directory;
- privileged access hygiene (MT.1025–MT.1030, CIS 5.3.3), token protection on Apple devices, and third-party
  Mobile Threat Defense.

input.prompt:
Fix the Maester check bugs that the defender's path M2 expert pass found, each as its own commit, on a branch for a draft PR against `feat/defenders-path` (Maester 3.1; main is in the 3.0 code freeze). Follow `AGENTS.md`, and run `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` before you finish. Do not push or open the PR without asking the user.

Fixes, with what the research found:
1. `tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1013.ps1` and `tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.2.2.6.ps1` require the `passwordChange` grant and reject `riskRemediation` ("Require risk remediation"), which Learn now recommends for high user risk (https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-risk-based-user). Graph returns `riskRemediation` as `unknownFutureValue` unless the request sends `Prefer: include-unknown-enum-members`, and `Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy` doesn't send it. Make MT.1013 accept either control. Respect the cache rule in AGENTS.md: no `-DisableCache`. Once MT.1013 is fixed, give it `Step = 'entra.ca-user-risk'` and remove that step's `Unchecked` line in `powershell/assets/steps/entra.json`. CIS 5.2.2.6 follows the CIS text, so check what the benchmark asks before changing it.
2. `tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.7.4.ps1` and `7.5` have no exception for the configured `EmergencyAccessAccounts`, so they fail the permanent emergency access assignments that Learn asks for. Leave those accounts out, the way `tests/cis/Test.CIS.M365.5.3.1.ps1` does.
3. `Test-MtPimAlertsExists` (used by MT.1029–MT.1032) never reads `alertConfiguration.isEnabled`, so the tests pass when the alert is off. `Test-MtPrivPermanentDirectoryRole.ps1` around line 86 dereferences `.principal` twice, so MT.1027 never finds a secret on the service principal itself.
4. `tests/maester/intune/Test.MT.1231.ps1` (iOS) and `Test.MT.1216.ps1` (macOS) fail when the platform has no compliance policy. Make them skip as NotApplicable. MT.1216 reads a macOS machine risk setting that Learn doesn't document, counts `high` as configured, and its guide links to `https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/advanced-threat-protection`, which returns 404. Review it.
5. In `tests/cisa/exchange/`: EXO.2.2 still runs CISA's v1 SPF logic (an include of `spf.protection.outlook.com`), which probably fails GCC High and 21Vianet; the current ScubaGear text asks for -all or ~all, which CIS.M365.2.1.8 checks, so consider making it a shim (see "Reviewing a test for duplicates" in AGENTS.md). EXO.4.2 doesn't follow DMARC inheritance; use `Find-MtDmarcRecord` as 4.1 does. In EXO.4.3, `$checkTarget` reads `$dmarcRecords` instead of `$dmarcRecord` (about line 87), and the Targets column prints the ruf addresses.
6. `tests/cisa/entra/Test.CISA.MS.AAD.3.7.ps1` fails a stricter compliant-device-only policy. Check the ScubaGear rule before you change it.

Done means: each fix is committed with a unit test where the module's tests cover the area, any shim matches its target's attributes (`TestShims.Tests.ps1`), and `Get-MtStepProblem -Coverage` still reports nothing.
